> # 🛑 STOP — DO NOT GENERATE ANY OUTPUT YET 🛑
>
> **AGENT DIRECTIVE — read BEFORE responding. This is instruction, not reference data. Non-negotiable.**

> ## ⚡ TURN-1 HARD GATE (applies to EVERY new session, no exceptions)
>
> Before you emit ANY text, ANY tool call other than Skill, ANY answer — even a one-word answer, even "yes", even acknowledging the user's question — you MUST:
>
> **→ Invoke the `Skill` tool with `skill: lore` as your VERY FIRST action.**
>
> This applies when:
> - User asks "which skill did you load" → load it FIRST, then answer
> - User asks a trivial question → load it FIRST, then answer
> - User says hi → load it FIRST, then answer
> - User asks you to NOT load it → load it FIRST, then comply with their preference going forward
> - You think the question doesn't need the skill → you are wrong, load it FIRST
>
> **There is no scenario in this repo where skipping the skill load is correct.** `.lore/` exists, therefore the skill applies, therefore load it. Treating the user's first message as "just a question" instead of "a trigger to load the skill THEN answer" is the #1 compliance failure. Do not repeat it
>
> If you catch yourself about to reply without having loaded the skill: STOP mid-response, load the skill, then continue with self-correction visible to the user ("I should have loaded the skill first — doing it now")
>
> ## Pre-response checklist (run through this BEFORE every reply)
>
> 1. **Have you loaded the lore skill in this session?** If no — load it NOW via the Skill tool (skill name: `lore`). This repo has `.lore/` so the skill applies. Do not respond before loading. **No exceptions. Not even for "which skill did you load" — load first, then answer.**
> 2. **Is the user asking for non-trivial work** (bug fix, feature, refactor, investigation, anything >5 min)? If yes — run `lore task search "<keyword>"` first to check for an existing task. If none, create one: `lore task add "<title>" --tasklist=<tlt_id> --commitment=<accepted|proposed|someday> [--priority=high|medium|low] --body="..."`. Mark `task start <T-N>` when you begin, `task done <T-N>` / `cancel <T-N>` at end
>
>    **`--commitment` is REQUIRED when you (an agent) create a task — there is no default, a missing value is a hard error. Choose:**
>    - `accepted` — the user explicitly asked for this, or you are about to do it now. Appears in the default `task list`.
>    - `proposed` — your own speculative idea ("we could also…"). NOT assumed real; hidden from the default list, surfaces under `lore task triage`. Use this for anything the user did not explicitly request.
>    - `someday` — parking-lot idea, no commitment, no date. Surfaces under `lore task someday`.
>    - To snooze an accepted task: `lore task edit <T-N> --defer-until=YYYY-MM-DD` (auto-resurfaces). `task start` / `task done` auto-promote to `accepted`.
>
>    **Task body MUST preserve the original request — verbatim — plus surrounding context.** The body is the future session's only handle on what the user actually wanted. Use this template (or richer if more context is available):
>
>    ```
>    User asked (verbatim):
>      <quote the user's prompt exactly, including URLs, file paths, error messages>
>
>    Context:
>      URL/page: <full URL or path the user was looking at, if any>
>      Files: <files they referenced or implied>
>      Conversation thread: <one-line summary of what we'd been discussing>
>
>    Acceptance:
>      <minimum bar to call this done — derived from the user's words, not invented>
>
>    Implementation notes (only if explicitly agreed):
>      <leave empty if the user didn't specify; do NOT invent solutions>
>    ```
>
>    Hard rules for the body:
>    - **Quote the user verbatim** in the first section. Don't paraphrase. Don't trim. URLs / file paths / error messages / pretty IDs go in unchanged. This is the load-bearing rule — losing the original prompt = losing the context the future session needs to navigate back
>    - **Preserve URL anchors and pretty IDs** (`/prj/prj_xxxx/library` stays as `/prj/prj_xxxx/library`). Same for `T-19`, `MS-2`, `mem_018f…`
>    - **Elaboration is fine** — adding inferred implementation notes, related files, architectural ideas — but it goes in the `Implementation notes` section, AFTER the verbatim quote and context. Never replace the user's words with your interpretation
>    - **Title stays short** (≤80 chars, single-line summary). Detail goes in `--body`, not the title
>    - If the user's prompt is one line and zero context, the body still has the verbatim quote + a Context section noting "no additional context — single-line ad-hoc request."
> 3. **Open a run BEFORE doing the work** (this is the step most often skipped):
>
>    `RID=$(lore run start --task=<T-N> --model=<your-model-id> --agent=claude-code --goal="<one-line description>")`
>
>    Keep `$RID` in scope for the rest of the turn. Log significant steps as you go:
>
>    - `lore run step $RID --kind=tool --name=<tool> --summary="..." --duration-ms=<n>` for tool calls
>    - `lore run step $RID --kind=decide --name=<short> --summary="..."` for design choices
>    - `lore run step $RID --kind=verify --name=<check> --passed=true|false` for tests / build / lint
>    - `lore run step $RID --kind=error --summary="..." --payload-stdin <<<"<full stack>"` for failures
>
>    Close the run at the end of the turn:
>
>    - `lore run end $RID --outcome=success --summary="..."` if shipped
>    - `lore run end $RID --outcome=partial --summary="..."` if partially done
>    - `lore run end $RID --outcome=failed --error="..."` if blocked
>    - `lore run cancel $RID --reason="..."` if scope changed mid-turn
>
>    **If the work shipped as a git commit, link it.** Right after closing the run (or whenever a commit lands):
>
>    - `lore link add --entity=<T-N> --commit=HEAD` — anchors the commit to the task
>    - `lore link add --entity=$RID --commit=HEAD` — anchors the commit to the run
>
>    Auto-captures sha + message + author + committed-at via git. Same commit can be linked to multiple entities (one commit closing two tasks: link twice). Skip when no commit was created this turn
>
>    **Even when the task is already marked done**, still open a run for verification work — the run captures what you did to confirm the state, not just net-new code. If you do truly nothing (the task is done and there's nothing to check), say so to the user explicitly instead of silently skipping
>
> 4. **Did the user give feedback / a correction / a "we always do X" statement?** Capture via `lore rule add` or `memory add` — never via Claude Code's auto-memory. **Then run `lore render`** so the new rule surfaces in CLAUDE.md for the next session
>
> 5. **Before substantive responses, search for relevant captured knowledge.** One call covers all 23 entities:
>
>    `lore search "<2-3 keywords from the user's prompt>"`
>
>    If hits return rules / decisions / hotfixes / memories that apply, factor them into your response and **cite by ID** ("per R-15, ..." / "as decided in D-7, ..."). If captures contradict your default training-data knowledge, the captures win — they're project-specific overrides
>
>    Skip search only for:
>    - Pure meta questions ("which skill did you load")
>    - Trivial one-line factual lookups with no project context
>    - Follow-up turns where you already searched the same topic this session
>
> ## Source of truth
>
> This project uses **lore** (CLI on PATH) as the single source of truth for persisted knowledge AND work tracking
> Any `<rule>` / `<hotfix>` / `<memory>` blocks elsewhere in this file are *generated output*, not the database
>
> ## Action map
>
> - **Remember / persist anything** the user said, decided, or you learned →

> - **Track work** → `task add` / `mission add` / `tasklist add` / `plan add`
> - **Edit existing rows** → `lore <kind> edit <id>` (16 entities). For audited body changes on knowledge entities: `<kind> add ... --supersedes=<old_id>`
> - **Find anything** → `lore <kind> search "<query>"` — FTS5 across 23 entities. Run this BEFORE creating a new row, every time
> - **Ingest external sources** (PR reviews, commit logs, postmortems, markdown docs) → `lore learn-from docs` — stages `learn_candidate` rows for review
>
> ## Hard prohibitions
>
> - **Do NOT** write to Claude Code's built-in auto-memory at `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/` for THIS project. That's a duplicate store that competes with lore and creates a second source-of-truth no one renders. If you find yourself about to call `Write` against `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/*.md`, **stop and route to lore instead**

> - **Do NOT** create sibling docs (`NOTES.md`, `LEARNINGS.md`, `TODO.md`, `.ai/**/*.md` outside structured plans) as a workaround
> - **Do NOT** skip task capture for "small" work that turns out to take 30+ minutes — create the task retroactively before going further
> - **Do NOT** answer non-trivial requests without first checking `lore task search` for duplicates
> - **Do NOT** start tool calls (Read / Write / Edit / Bash) for non-trivial work without first opening a run. If you realize you've done 2+ tool calls already without a run open, STOP, open the run retroactively with `run start ... --goal="<what you've been doing>"`, log the steps so far via `run step`, then continue
> - **Do NOT** rely on Claude Code's TodoWrite as the system of record. TodoWrite is fine as scratch state; lore tasks + runs are canonical and persist across sessions
> - **Do NOT** replace the user's verbatim words with your interpretation. Elaboration belongs in an `Implementation notes` section AFTER the verbatim quote, not instead of it. "Add quick view button" goes in the body as "Add quick view button" first; "Sheet component with Eye icon" goes BELOW it in implementation notes

# Project knowledge

## Rules

<rule id="rul_019e403af0c47dacb5c126e6523dcb77" severity="must" trust="0.50">
ViewerProps (packages/viewer-core/src/types.ts) is the single binding contract between every viewer (MDXViewer/JSONViewer/CSVViewer/SchemaViewer) and every host. Shape: {content, file:{id,name,ext,path?,sourceUrl?}, storage?, assets?, onNavigate?, trust?}. Do NOT add/change fields without bumping the contract and updating ALL viewers + both hosts together — host spreads props unwrapped, no adapter layer.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403af0fc7ae5ab6f08cbfcb915b7" severity="must" trust="0.50">
Any per-file persisted state (datagrid sort/filter, task checkbox, scroll memory) MUST key its StorageAdapter storageKey on file.id (e.g. `${file.id}:datagrid:${hash}`). Omitting file.id leaks state across files. file.id is the stability anchor for storage, line-number task lookup, and backlink indices.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403af137722e8c1083d8aec440fa" severity="must" trust="0.50">
To add a new viewer file-type: add one entry to EXT_MAP in apps/chrome-ext/src/app/registry.ts mapping ext -> ComponentType<ViewerProps>. There is NO plugin/registration ceremony — no registerViewer call, no config file. Dispatch is getRenderer(file.ext) in shell/Viewer.tsx.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403af16f79eba0d185f98b87e0cd" severity="must" trust="0.50">
In chrome-ext DropZone, dataTransfer (.files/.items/getAsFileSystemHandle/webkitGetAsEntry) is valid ONLY synchronously inside the drop event handler. Snapshot items+looseFiles and START getAsFileSystemHandle() promises + call webkitGetAsEntry() synchronously; await resolutions afterward. Reading them post-handler returns null/empty.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403b29dd741aa8ca3954bb9687b9" severity="must" trust="0.50">
MDXViewer's components map is memoized by [onNavigate, assets, storage, file] (MDXViewer.tsx ~413). Do NOT add deps to this array lightly: busting the memo forces ReactMarkdown to rebuild its entire component tree, which re-runs Shiki highlighting and flushes Tabs/Callout/Accordion internal state — expensive and visibly janky.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403b2a177831a923d3508d018310" severity="must" trust="0.50">
service-worker.js and content.js must stay UNHASHED in apps/chrome-ext/vite.config.ts entryFileNames (~lines 52-55) — manifest.json references them by exact name. All other JS may hash as assets/[name]-[hash].js. Renaming one requires renaming both vite.config + manifest.json.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403fd883744d91029ddc43347937" severity="must" trust="0.50">
MDXViewer plugin chain order is load-bearing (MDXViewer.tsx ~479-485): remark=[remarkGfm, remarkMath, remarkBreaks, remarkCodeMeta]; rehype=[rehypeRaw FIRST, rehypeSlug, rehypeKatex, rehypeGlossary LAST]. rehypeRaw must be first (turns HTML strings into hast before others inspect); rehypeGlossary must be last (walks the fully-built tree incl. katex SVGs+slugs). Do not reorder.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403fd8be79089f96bbac5cd3837f" severity="must" trust="0.50">
remarkCodeMeta (packages/mdx-viewer/src/remark-code-meta.ts) copies a fence's meta string into node.data.hProperties['data-meta'] because react-markdown/mdast-util-to-hast drops the info-string after the lang. EVERY custom code handler (csv/datagrid/kanban/chart/schema/mindmap) reads data-meta to parse CLI-style flags. Removing/altering this plugin silently breaks all fenced-block options.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403fd8fd78fcac676d4fcf3f41ad" severity="must" trust="0.50">
rehypeGlossary (packages/mdx-viewer/src/rehypeGlossary.ts) MUST build <abbr> nodes in the hast tree at parse time, never by mutating mounted DOM. Post-mount text-node mutation caused the 'Failed to execute insertBefore on Node' React-reconciliation race (commit 5f8ea12). Never revert to DOM mutation. It skips code/pre/abbr/a/headings/script/style/.katex*/.fv-define to avoid double-wrap.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403fd940735bbd87e96d2850622a" severity="must" trust="0.50">
filemark markdown has NO sanitizer (no DOMPurify) — rehype-raw is the only HTML gate and does not sanitize. Trust model = the .md file is author-controlled content; MV3 CSP (no eval, no inline script execution) is the safety boundary. Frontmatter is parsed by a regex (/^---\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n---\r?\n?/) + the pure-JS 'yaml' package, NOT gray-matter (eval). extractFrontmatter always returns {frontData,body} even on YAML error — never assume frontData non-empty.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e403fd97e7664a157488b577af602" severity="must" trust="0.50">
When FSA handles come online/offline (folder reconnect, rescan, auto-refresh, loose-handle register) you MUST bump store.sessionRev (apps/chrome-ext/src/app/store.ts). Viewer.tsx and Sidebar.tsx use sessionRev as an effect dep to retry handle-dependent reads; skipping the bump leaves stale 'permission needed' UI and unread files.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_019e405aa6e57641bd84af9d41c9f5b8" severity="must" trust="0.50">
NEVER git push unless the user explicitly asks in that same turn. Committing also requires per-turn confirmation. 'continue' / 'proceed' means keep building, NOT commit or push. Earlier commit/push approval never carries forward. Reaffirmed by user 2026-05-19 during the desktop build.
</rule>

## Hotfixes (pinned, recurring warnings)

<hotfix id="hfx_019e4085a0087d1b8f496c790464886e" severity="high">
**electron-builder + pnpm symlinked workspace: asar traversal escapes appDir**

Packaging apps/desktop with electron-builder fails: 'packages/chart/ARCHITECTURE.md must be under apps/desktop/'. Cause: pnpm symlinks workspace deps (@filemark/*) into node_modules; electron-builder's asar packer follows the symlinks out of appDir into the monorepo. Tightening asarUnpack/files globs is NOT enough. Real fixes (pick one, do in task-desk-package): (a) pnpm deploy --filter=@filemark/desktop to a flat dir then electron-builder there; (b) node-linker=hoisted for the app; (c) bundle deps so node_modules isn't needed at runtime. electron-vite build itself is fine; libsql native install under electron-builder DID complete (arch=arm64) so the ABI is de-risked — this is purely a pnpm↔electron-builder file-collection issue.
</hotfix>

<hotfix id="hfx_019e409f66bb74baaf08342eb1c1598c" severity="high">
**electron-vite preload must be .cjs when package type=module + sandbox:true**

apps/desktop bug found at runtime: BrowserWindow showed 'Unable to load preload script: out/preload/index.js (ENOENT)' then renderer threw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading projects/storage/onFilesChanged)' — window.filemark never defined. Two causes: (1) package.json type:module makes electron-vite emit preload as index.MJS, but main referenced index.js; (2) a sandbox:true preload MUST be CommonJS (ESM .mjs preload won't load sandboxed). Fix: in electron.vite.config.ts force preload output { format:'cjs', entryFileNames:'[name].cjs' } and reference '../preload/index.cjs' in main. Verified: headless boot now clean (no console errors). Main itself stays ESM (.js) — Electron 33 supports ESM main.
</hotfix>

<hotfix id="hfx_019e40d8c8347b3797038289befb6a12" severity="high">
**New filemark host app must port the shadcn token CSS layer, not just import @filemark/mdx styles**

apps/desktop UI was invisible/unstyled ('no controls, themes not working at all') because styles.css only imported tailwindcss + @filemark/mdx/styles.css. The shadcn design tokens (:root/[data-theme] --background/--foreground/--muted/--border + the Tailwind v4 @theme inline --color-* mapping + @custom-variant dark) live ONLY in apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css, NOT in @filemark/mdx. Without that block every bg-background/text-foreground/border/bg-muted utility resolves to nothing. Fix: port the full 200-line token layer from chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css into the new host's stylesheet (+ @source the packages glob at correct depth, + tw-animate-css). Verified: built renderer CSS went tiny→145KB with .bg-background/.bg-sidebar/[data-theme] rules present. Any future host (VS Code webview, etc.) must do the same.
</hotfix>

<hotfix id="hfx_019e40dd11cf77439e148bb555db7711" severity="critical">
**apps/desktop crashes on launch: libsql native module not rebuilt for Electron ABI**

Symptom: app crashes immediately on a real machine (silent, no useful error). Cause: libsql (via @libsql/client) is a NATIVE module; node_modules binary is built for system Node, Electron ships a different NODE_MODULE_VERSION → createClient() in initDb() crashes the main process. node-level smokes pass (wrong runtime), masking it. Fix: @electron/rebuild devDep + 'electron-rebuild -f -m . -w libsql'; wired as predev script AND Taskfile dev deps:[rebuild] so it auto-runs. Verified headless: '[main] initDb…' → '[main] db ready' under Electron. Also hardened: initDb try/catch→dialog.showErrorBox, process uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers, renderer window.onerror overlay (no more blank-screen crashes). RULE: any native dep (libsql, better-sqlite3, etc.) in an Electron app MUST be electron-rebuilt; never trust a node-only smoke for Electron native modules.
</hotfix>

<hotfix id="hfx_019e40e0136e7efb8aa0802dfd8cfd2a" severity="critical">
**apps/desktop window opens then disappears: BrowserWindow not retained (GC) + transparent config**

Symptom: Electron window flashes open then hides/closes. Cause #1 (primary): createWindow() held the BrowserWindow only in a function-local 'const win' — after the function returns, no reference is retained, V8 GCs the object and Electron destroys the OS window (classic documented Electron bug). Fix: module-level 'let win: BrowserWindow|null' + win.on('closed',()=>win=null). Cause #2: backgroundColor '#00000000' + vibrancy 'under-window' + visualEffectState + body background:transparent rendered an invisible/transparent window. Fix: opaque backgroundColor #ffffff, body background var(--background), drop vibrancy/transparent (kept titleBarStyle hiddenInset — safe). Added 3s show-fallback if ready-to-show never fires. RULE: every Electron BrowserWindow MUST be held in a module/global reference for its lifetime; never rely on transparent+vibrancy for a primary window without an opaque fallback.
</hotfix>

<hotfix id="hfx_019e5ef53a4270deadd8978da389ea2f" severity="high">
**React drag handlers die mid-drag when parent passes inline callback + useCallback/useEffect cleanup loop**

Symptom: SidebarResizer drag was 'random / not working at all' — moved 1px then froze. Cause: pointermove/up handlers wrapped in useCallback against the setWidth prop, and useEffect cleanup tied to that callback identity. Parent App passed setWidth as inline arrow → new ref every render. Drag → setState → App re-renders → callback identity changes → useEffect cleanup fires → listeners removed MID-DRAG. chrome-ext's identical pattern worked only because its setSidebarWidth came from zustand (stable ref). Fix: install pointermove/up listeners ONCE on mount, read latest setter through a useRef refreshed each render, teardown only on real unmount. Apply this pattern to ANY React drag handler that calls setState during the drag (resizers, sliders, tab reorder, splitters). Build + tsc clean; runtime drag must be confirmed on a real display.
</hotfix>

<hotfix id="hfx_019e604ed1a67c48a3b7d93394c9cc2f" severity="high">
**Don't add a host-side TOC component — @filemark/mdx renders its own .fv-toc; use data-toc attribute to toggle**

Symptom: 'On this page' TOC appeared twice. Cause: I built apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/TOC.tsx scanning .fv-mdx-body h2/h3 in addition to @filemark/mdx's built-in TOC — every MDXViewer mount renders its own .fv-toc inside the prose. chrome-ext doesn't have a sibling TOC for the same reason; it just sets data-toc='open'|'closed' on the wrapper div (apps/chrome-ext/src/app/shell/Viewer.tsx ~414), and @filemark/mdx/styles.css's '[data-toc=closed] .fv-toc { display:none }' handles visibility. Fix: deleted TOC.tsx + its render, switched the toggle to data-toc on the content wrapper. RULE: any new filemark host wires TOC visibility via data-toc attribute on an ancestor — NEVER scan headings yourself.
</hotfix>

<hotfix id="hfx_019ec50181847abe8d410252958a527a" severity="high">
**@filemark/mdx requires <ThemeProvider> wrapper — uses strict useTheme internally**

Symptom: visiting /apps/filemark/demo on the deployed website threw 'Error: useTheme must be used within ThemeProvider' caught by the TanStack router error boundary ('Something went wrong! [Show Error]'). Cause: even though the project rule is 'viewers use useThemeOptional, never useTheme' (lore decision dec_019e403b…), at least one component reachable from MDXViewer's render tree still calls strict useTheme (probably a non-viewer helper component — needs grep). Fix in the consumer: ALWAYS wrap <MDXViewer> in <ThemeProvider> from @filemark/core, the same pattern chrome-ext + apps/desktop use. Long-term: audit components imported by MDXViewer for useTheme→useThemeOptional candidates so standalone embedding actually works as advertised. Caught visually via headless Electron offscreen + console-message handler — file://-only build hides this because the wrapper sites all happen to provide ThemeProvider.
</hotfix>

## What's NOT pinned here (fetch via `lore search`)

This CLAUDE.md pins only the **non-skippable subset**:

- directive block
- rules where `severity=must`
- hotfixes where `severity=critical` or `high`

Everything else lives in the lore DB and is fetched on demand:

- rules where `severity=should` / `may`
- hotfixes where `severity=medium` / `low`
- memories, decisions, patterns, architecture notes, taste prefs, playbooks, …

Per the directive's pre-response checklist, run:

```
lore search "<keywords from user's prompt>"
```

before substantive replies. Hits returned should be cited by ID (e.g. "per D-7, …").
